newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey invites bids for 44 hydraulic power plants.
newsitem.headline: Turkey invites bids for 44 hydraulic power plants.

text.p: Turkey, in a massive energy generation drive to close deficits, invited bids on Friday for 44 small-size power plants with a total capacity of 4,477 MegaWatts (MW) and 14.5 billion kiloWatt-hours (kWh) of annual power output, energy ministry said.
It said in an announcement in the Official Gazette that companies would have to submit their bids by February, April and June, 1997, depending on the power plant they intend to build.
It said the plants would be built on a build-operate-transfer (BOT) basis, devised in the 1980s requiring the builders to provide finances themselves for big infrastructure projects.

Energy officials said the 44 power plants would be in addition to 11 others, for which the ministry invited tenders on September 24 and are to be designed to produce a total of 9.29 billion kWh annually from a total capacity of 2,688 MW.
Officials said the entire 55 plants could be completed in four or five years and help Turkey close energy deficits.

Turkey began importing electricity from Iran to close deficits in August at an initial 25 MW level through an existing grid. Officials said imports would rise to 100 MW next year and reach an eventual 720 MW after improvements in the existing lines and construction of new lines between the two countries.
Turkey, which expects to produce 93.1 billion kWh this year against a consumption of 97.5 billion kWh, has also been in talks with Georgia and Bulgaria to import electricity.
